reviewer.notes: Cross-vendor re-derivation from live probe files, not from the harvest UNIT-COMPLETE badge. Probe 1 re-ran the fixture installer: non-revoked controls succeeded on every source; post-revoke live and lockfile refused MKT-I04; stale cache/export/mirror silently installed. Probe 2 inspected source metadata and schemas: live revocation list carries the target, stale snapshots do not, lockfile/mirror/offline have no freshness contract. Catalog P1 rows remain product residuals; they are waived-by-owner for receipt condition 10 and stay CONFIRMED in report.verdicts_by_target.

defects.summary: A pre-revocation offline export and mirror silently install the revoked version; neither source has a freshness/expiry contract. The local-cache filesystem surrogate behaves the same.
A pre-deprecation offline export and mirror silently install without a warning or allow-deprecated marker. The local-cache filesystem surrogate behaves the same.
platform/marketplace/mkt has no cache source implementation, so the cache arm is a filesystem-registry snapshot surrogate and remains PARTIAL for a production cache path.

residual_unknowns.claim: The measured timings are one-process local fixture timings, not a network propagation distribution.

report.question_or_target: After a package version is revoked or deprecated in the registry, can it still be installed from a local cache, a lockfile pin, an offline export or a mirror - and how long is the propagation delay?
report.answer: Yes from the pre-change offline export and mirror, silently; the cache-format surrogate also succeeds but the shipped marketplace has no cache adapter. No from the frozen lockfile path when it remains attached to the changed live registry. Stale sources have no bounded delay because no refresh, TTL, expiry or last-sync contract exists.
